ratings.reason: It is a test-gating action using an independent oracle for duplicates, omissions, retries, and latency, not a browse mechanism that violates constraints.
It freezes membership at a committed version fence with birth/death versions, tombstones, signed expiry cursor, and keyset pagination while avoiding cross-request transactions.
It promises IDs existing at a committed fence, excludes later inserts, returns tombstones for later deletes, and adds bounded scans and expiry within retained history.
It defines the session dataset as committed-version S membership with later deletions represented by retained tombstones and tests exact equality and uniqueness.
It uses a committed watermark with creation/deletion versions and tombstones so eligible IDs are traversed exactly once with later inserts excluded.

It precisely offers a weaker deletion-sensitive contract: excludes post-start inserts but intentionally omits records deleted before their page read, with keyset cursors and an oracle for that contract.
A copy-on-write ordered membership tree in the existing store could define a pinned root, but atomic root publication, retention, and 300 ms behavior are unsupported operational dependencies.

The pinned copy-on-write ID tree is implementable in outline, but feasibility is conservative because write amplification, publication contention, reclamation, and latency are not established for the existing store.

It materializes an expiring ordered ID manifest in the existing store from watermark membership, publishes only complete manifests, returns deletion markers, and tests equality, multiplicity, and latency.
